key_insight: TensorMutation learns transferable weight-space effects of fault-informed training mutations, enabling mutant generation without retraining each model.
engineering_relevance: A reusable mutation predictor could reduce the computational cost of deep-learning mutation testing while approximating realistic training faults.
method: Represent a trained model as a neural graph.
Use a mutation-conditioned GNN to predict parameter changes.
Train offline on original–mutant pairs and reuse across unseen models.
evidence_signal: Using 25,252 pairs from 71 MLP classifiers and 11 mutation operators, TensorMutation partially reproduced mutation behavior on nine held-out subjects and achieved the highest median behavioral similarity on 12 real-fault subjects.
watch_item: Evidence is limited to MLP classifiers; real-fault similarity improved significantly over DeepMutation++ but not over DeepCrime or a norm-matched random control.
paper_title: TensorMutation: Learning Weight-Space Mutations of Deep Learning Models on Neural Graphs
